newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan orders bank to halt operations.
newsitem.headline: Japan orders bank to halt operations.

text.p: For the first time in 51 years, Japanese regulators on Thursday ordered a bank to halt most operations, the latest embarrassment to the nation's financial sector.
A senior Finance Ministry official told Reuters that Hanwa Bank Ltd was being ordered to suspend all its operations except deposit withdrawals because it was unable to recover bad loans.

The regional bank, employing about 900 people and operating mostly in western Japan around the city of Osaka, would be the first bank to come under a government suspension order since the end of World War two in 1945.
The official said details of the bank's troubles would be announced at a news conference later on Thursday.
But deposits at the bank would be fully protected, the official said.
Established in 1941, the bank has book assets of about 658 billion yen ($5.92 billion). It is not one of Japan's "big 20" first tier national banks

Like much of Japan's financial system, Hanwa Bank has been hard hit by the collapse of mainly real estate prices from the sky-high levels of the 1980's so-called "bubble" era when the country's economy was in full steam.

"The ministry made the decision following the judgment that Hanwa Bank will most likely incur about 30 billion yen ($270 million) in liabilities, or an excess of liabilities over assets, in the (April-September) first half of fiscal 1996/97, making it extremely difficult to turn around on its own," Kyodo news service said.
On November 5, Hanwa announced that it had revised its forecast for parent current earnings for the first half of the current fiscal year to a loss of 280 million yen ($2.52 million).

Previously, the bank had forecast parent current profit of 60 million yen ($540,000) for the first half of 1996/97 against actual 232 million yen ($2.09 million) in current profit a year earlier. In 1995/96 ended March 31, 1996, however, it posted current loss of 6.55 billion yen ($59.0 million).
Current profit is pre-tax, including profits or losses from stock selling and other non-banking business.
Last year Japan went through its first bank failure since the war when Hyogo Bank, also based in western Japan in Kobe adjacent to Osaka, was a victim of bad loans.
The news of Hanwa Bank's shutdown played into currency markets.

In New York, the dollar had dipped under 111 yen on the back of the wider U.S. trade deficit but then recovered to 111.70 on hearing the news about Hanwa bank as traders speculated Japanese financial authorities would push interest rates lower to help the country's financial institutions.
